summary: National Credit Code (Schedule 1 to the National Consumer Credit Protection Act 2009). Bound: Credit providers and debtors under credit contracts regulated by the Code (s 72 text refers to 'the credit provider'; s 89A applies to a credit provider required to give a default notice under s 88).

clauses.heading: Changes on grounds of hardship: hardship notice
clauses.text: If a debtor considers that he or she is or will be unable to meet his or her obligations under a credit contract, the debtor may give the credit provider notice (a hardship notice), orally or in writing, of the debtor's inability to meet the obligations.
clauses.notes: Provision read: s 72(1). A hardship notice can be given orally, so a customer telling a chat or voice agent 'I can't make my repayments' may be a hardship notice. An agent that fails to recognise it, insists it must be in writing, or does not route it starts the statutory clock without the provider knowing.

clauses.heading: Notice of decision on changing credit contract
clauses.text: The credit provider must ... give the debtor a notice: ... (b) that is in the form (if any) prescribed by the regulations and states: (i) the credit provider and the debtor have not agreed ...; and (ii) the reasons why ...; and (iii) the name and contact details of the AFCA scheme
clauses.notes: Provision read: s 72(4). An agent that refuses hardship on the spot without reasons or AFCA details, or that loses the request so no decision notice issues within the s 72(5) period (generally 21 days), causes a breach. Civil penalty 5,000 penalty units.

clauses.heading: Effect of hardship notices on enforcement
clauses.text: The credit provider must not begin enforcement proceedings against the debtor unless: (a) the credit provider has given the debtor a notice under paragraph 72(4)(b), in response to the current hardship notice, stating that the credit provider and debtor have not agreed to change the credit contract; and (b) the period of 14 days ... has expired.
clauses.notes: Provision read: s 89A(2). A collections agent that threatens or initiates repossession or legal action while a hardship notice is pending (no s 72(4)(b) notice plus 14 days) misstates the provider's rights and can trigger a strict liability offence.
